title: Fact-check effect by topic
rationale: In the source study fact-checks were shared 13.3 points less overall, but E2 shows the health estimate near zero (-0.028, SE 0.028) against about -0.15 for political items, with only about 1,100 health profiles and topic not randomized. Randomizing topic with a balanced item bank tests whether the penalty really differs by topic, and survey language is added because of language differences.
contribution: Provides a randomized, adequately powered test of whether the fact-check sharing penalty holds for health as for political claims, in English and Spanish.
limitations: Single-post sharing with an opt-out differs from the forced-pair choice of the source study.
Item content differs between topics even in a balanced bank; topic effects may reflect item features.
Spanish-language respondents are self-selected into language and language is not randomized.
Hypothetical sharing, not behavior on a platform.

design.title: Fact-check sharing penalty: health versus political claims
design.overview: US adults, with Spanish-language respondents oversampled, are randomized to a topic (health or political). Each sees several posts from a bank of at least 20 items per topic, each shown as true/neutral, misinformation, or fact-check, and chooses whether to share or not share.
design.hypothesis: The fact-check sharing penalty relative to true/neutral posts is smaller for health than for political items. Misinformation is shared less than true content in both topics. Exploratory: the topic difference varies by survey language.
design.primaryOutcome: Share choice for each post (share vs. do not share), with an opt-out.
design.comparison: Fact-check versus true/neutral sharing, compared between health and political topic arms; information type varies within respondent.
design.population: US adults 18+ recruited from an online panel, with Spanish-language respondents oversampled; survey offered in English or Spanish.

conditions.title: Health topic
conditions.description: Respondent sees health posts only: true/neutral, misinformation and fact-check items.

conditions.title: Political topic
conditions.description: Respondent sees political posts only: true/neutral, misinformation and fact-check items.

questions.text: This survey asks about how you would respond to posts on social media. It takes about 10 minutes and is voluntary. Do you agree to participate?
In which language are you completing this survey?
You will see six posts about health. For each, tell us whether you would share it.
You will see six posts about politics. For each, tell us whether you would share it.

Thank you. Some posts you saw were false, and some were fact-checks correcting false claims. They were shown for research only. Please rely on reliable health and news sources for accurate information.

assumptions: Power target: about 1200 per arm to detect 0.04 at 80% power; E2 health fact-check -0.028 (SE 0.028) versus political -0.151; difference of about 0.12 is detectable, but 0.04 targets a smaller health effect; MDE 0.031 at n~4,000 per arm.
Total about 2,400 or more, with at least 600 Spanish-language respondents; standard errors clustered by respondent and item random effects.
Three posts per respondent are shown here for brevity; the full version would show about six per topic with information type randomized per item, to fit 10 minutes.
Information type is assigned randomly per post, balanced across the item bank of at least 20 items per topic; each item exists in all three versions where possible.
Spanish items are professionally translated and back-translated.
unresolved: The item bank (at least 20 health and 20 political items in true, false and fact-check versions) and Spanish translations must be supplied by the research team.
Per-post randomization of information type is implemented in the survey platform; the embedded stimulus slots show one draw.
Panel vendor, compensation and IRB approval number need to be supplied.
